extracted.intended_audience: late-night comedy writers and aspiring topical joke writers (Daily Show staff or similar writers' rooms)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing and evaluating topical jokes in a late-night satirical writers' room, covering process pipeline, required factual reporting, joke structure/escalation, host-voice fit, rehearsal validation, and content-sensitivity checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily Show Joke Pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Seven-step daily production timeline: Morning meeting (9am) → Reporting (10am-noon) → Writing (noon-3pm) → Rewrite (3-5pm) → Rehearsal (5-6pm) → Tape (6:30pm) → Air (11pm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each step is a production and quality-control checkpoint: morning meeting for story-angle pitches; reporting/research desk validates premises; writing produces drafts; rewrite/punch-up in the room; rehearsal produces cuts based on host read and audience reaction; tape captures performance and audience response; the show airs as an edited final. Timing disciplines when and how material is developed and tested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical Joke Format
rubrics_metrics.description: A typical joke block contains: News-line setup (factual, neutral), Reaction beat (host's face / aside), Joke 1 (broad, accessible), Joke 2 (deeper / more specific), Joke 3 (absurdist tag).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three-joke escalation gives the audience three on-ramps into the same premise—broad to specific to absurd—so different audience members can 'get in' at different levels. Use a factual neutral setup and a reaction beat to cue the host's viewpoint before escalating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting-First Discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Daily Show writes from FACTS, not assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jokes that depend on wrong facts will be cut. The research desk validates premises and functions as part of joke quality control; confirm details before committing a joke to script or on-air. This discipline prevents factual errors that can ruin a joke's effectiveness or credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host's Persona Fit
rubrics_metrics.description: A joke must fit the host's voice/persona.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different hosts use different fuels: Stewart-era jokes leaned on moral indignation; Noah-era jokes leverage outsider observation. The same factual premise requires different jokes depending on the host—write to the host's sensibility and delivery style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dead On Arrival (DOA) List
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics so heavy or so recent that NO joke would land are placed on a DOA list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such topics are always cut before air; this is treated as a kindness to the audience. The DOA list is a preemptive content-sensitivity filter used across the pipeline to avoid trying to force humor where it would be inappropriate or harmful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the joke based on a verified fact?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the joke based on a verified fact?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a primary quality gate: verification happens at the reporting/research stage and is re-checked before air. If the underlying fact is incorrect, the joke will be cut regardless of cleverness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the joke fit the host's persona?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the joke fit the host's persona?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the joke aligns with the host's established voice and rhetorical tendencies (e.g., moral indignation vs. outsider observation). Host-read comfort and authenticity affect whether a joke survives rewrite and rehearsal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there a tonal escalation across three jokes?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a tonal escalation across three jokes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for the broad→specific→absurd progression (or equivalent escalation) so the bit offers multiple on-ramps and a satisfying payoff. The three-joke structure is an intentional pacing/tonal rubric used in the writers' room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has the room punched it up beyond the writer's draft?
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the room punched it up beyond the writer's draft?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material is expected to be improved by the rewrite/punch-up process (3-5pm). The writers' room collaborates to sharpen jokes; a draft that hasn't been punched up may be seen as underdeveloped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has it been cut for content that's too heavy / too soon?
rubrics_metrics.description: Has it been cut for content that's too heavy / too soon?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check the DOA list and recent events: if a topic is judged too sensitive or recent, cut it regardless of quality. Sensitivity and timing are active evaluative criteria in deciding what goes to air.

rubrics_metrics.name: Did the audience laugh in rehearsal?
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the audience laugh in rehearsal?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearsal (5-6pm) is a live test—audience reaction and host read influence cuts. Positive rehearsal response is a practical validation; lack of laughter commonly results in rework or removal before tape.
